# loopway

> loopway is a notification system for your bots. Webhooks from the services you use land in one inbox as CloudEvents, and your own code reads them.

If a person asks you to set up loopway, the steps are below. Everything is done with the `loopway` CLI, which talks to {{base_url}}.

## Concepts

- **Inbox**: every user has one, with one URL. Messages stay for 14 days.
- **Source**: something the inbox accepts, named by its type: `github`, `linear`, `vercel`, `granola`, `resend`, `schedule` (messages on a clock) or `loopway` (messages sent with a token). A webhook source stores the sender's signing secret. A delivery no source verifies is refused.
- **Message**: one stored delivery: the CloudEvent (its `type`, e.g. `com.github.issues.opened`, and `data`) and when it arrived. Nothing is marked done.
- **Reader**: a JS file whose default export takes one message. `loopway read` calls it for each new message, in order. If it throws, that message comes again. Delivery is at least once, so dedupe on `msg.message_id` if a repeat would do harm.

## Setup

```bash
curl -fsSL {{base_url}}/install.sh | sh
loopway login
loopway source register github
loopway inbox                    # the URL to add in the sender
```

For `vercel`, `linear`, `granola` and `resend` the sender makes the secret: register, add the webhook there, then run `loopway source update <source> --secret <secret>`.

## Reading

```js
// reader.js
export default async function (msg, ctx) {
  if (msg.type.startsWith("com.github.")) console.log(msg.type, msg.subject);
}
```

```bash
loopway read reader.js             # everything since the last read
loopway poll reader.js             # the same, until stopped
loopway read reader.js --since 2h  # go back: a time, microseconds since the epoch, or how long ago
loopway messages list              # the newest messages
loopway messages get <message> --data
loopway push build.done --data '{"ok":true}'
```

## MCP

`{{base_url}}/api/mcp` is a hosted MCP server with `push_message` and `pull_messages` tools. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, using a token from `loopway token create <name>`.
